question: What regulatory actions may follow if aflatoxin levels exceed the applicable maximum level?
shared_benchmark_context:
All questions belong to one fixed EU food-regulation benchmark concerning the same case:
a shipment of dried figs originating from Türkiye in which aflatoxin B1 has been detected.

Q1–Q10 form one regulatory-assessment sequence. Answer only the current question, but when
the wording refers to “if so”, “the assessment”, “major conclusions”, “the evidence above”,
or similar cross-question references, interpret those references within this shared benchmark case.

Across the sequence, the regulatory issues being examined include:
relevant EU legislation, contaminant limits, product-use/processing distinctions,
import controls and documentation, responsible actors, possible regulatory actions,
and which conclusions require current-law verification.

Do not assume shipment-specific facts that are not stated in the current question or supplied evidence.
Do not invent legal provisions, numerical limits, or documentary requirements.
shared_system_prompt:
You are evaluating an EU food-regulation question.

Answer conservatively and distinguish:
1. what is supported,
2. what remains uncertain or requires verification.

Do not invent legal provisions, numerical limits, or documentary requirements.

Use this structure:
## 1. Short answer
## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions
## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed
build03_tool_rules:
You have access to search_regulation, which searches only the frozen five-law library.
Use it for substantive legal claims. If evidence is incomplete, you may search again
with a narrower or complementary query. Do not invent legal provisions, numbers,
mandatory actions, or requirements. Distinguish border-stage measures from
post-market operator duties if the evidence supports both.
Treat the local library as a historical snapshot; do not imply it proves current law.
Cite regulation number and precise article/annex when the retrieved text supports them.
Do not assume missing facts about the specific consignment.

results.heading: Withdrawal of the designation of border control posts
results.text: Article 62 Withdrawal of the designation of border control posts 1. Where border control posts cease to comply with the requirements referred to in Article 64, the Member States shall: (a) withdraw the designation provided for in Article 59(1) for all or for certain categories of animals and goods for which the designation was made; and (b) remove those border control posts from the lists referred to in Article 60(1), for the categories of animals and goods for which the designation is withdrawn. 2. Member States shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of the withdrawal of the designation of a border control post as provided for in paragraph 1 and of the reasons for such withdrawal. 3. The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 144 to supplement this Regulation concerning the cases where, and the procedures by which, border control posts for which the designation has only been partially withdrawn in accordance with point (a) of paragraph 1 of this Article may be re-designated by way of derogation from Article 59. 4. This Article shall be without prejudice to Member States’ competence to decide on the withdrawal of designation of border control posts for reasons other than those referred to in this Regulation.

results.location: Article 63 — Suspension of the designation of border control posts
results.heading: Suspension of the designation of border control posts
results.text: Article 63 Suspension of the designation of border control posts 1. A Member State shall suspend the designation of a border control post and order its activities to be stopped, for all or for certain categories of animals and goods for which the designation was made, in cases where such activities may result in a risk to human, animal or plant health, animal welfare or, as regards GMOs and plant protection products, also to the environment. In the case of a serious risk, the suspension shall be with immediate effect. 2. Member States shall immediately inform the Commission and the other Member States of any suspension of the designation of a border control post and the reasons for such a suspension. 3. Member States shall indicate the suspension of the designation of a border control post in the lists referred to in Article 60(1). 4. Member States shall remove the suspension provided for in paragraph 1 as soon as: (a) the competent authorities are satisfied that the risk referred to in paragraph 1 no longer exists; and (b) they have communicated to the Commission and to the other Member States the information on the basis of which the suspension is removed. 5. This Article shall be without prejudice to Member States’ competence to decide on the suspension of designation of border control posts for reasons other than those referred to in this Regulation.

results.location: Article 64 — Minimum requirements for border control posts
results.heading: Minimum requirements for border control posts
results.text: Article 64 Minimum requirements for border control posts 1. Border control posts shall be located in the immediate vicinity of the point of entry into the Union and either in a place which is designated by the customs authorities in accordance with Article 135(1) and (2) of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 or in a free zone. 2. The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 144 to supplement this Regulation concerning the cases where and conditions under which a border control post may be situated at a distance other than in the immediate vicinity of the point of entry into the Union in cases of specific geographical constraints. 3. Border control posts shall have: (a) a sufficient number of suitably qualified staff; (b) premises or other facilities appropriate to the nature and volume of the categories of animals and goods handled; (c) equipment and premises or other facilities to allow the performance of official controls for each of the categories of animals and goods for which the border control post has been designated; (d) arrangements in place to ensure, as appropriate, access to any other equipment, premise and service necessary to apply the measures taken in accordance with Articles 65, 66 and 67 in cases of suspicion of non-compliance, non-compliant consignments or consignments presenting a risk; (e) contingency arrangements to ensure the smooth operation of official controls and the effective application of the measures taken in accordance with Articles 65, 66 and 67 in cases of unforeseeable and unexpected conditions or events; (f) the technology and equipment necessary for the efficient operation of the IMSOC and, as appropriate, of other computerised information management systems necessary for the handling and exchange of data

results.heading: Food safety requirements
results.text: Article 14 Food safety requirements 1. Food shall not be placed on the market if it is unsafe. 2. Food shall be deemed to be unsafe if it is considered to be: (a) injurious to health; (b) unfit for human consumption. 3. In determining whether any food is unsafe, regard shall be had: (a) to the normal conditions of use of the food by the consumer and at each stage of production, processing and distribution, and (b) to the information provided to the consumer, including information on the label, or other information generally available to the consumer concerning the avoidance of specific adverse health effects from a particular food or category of foods. 4. In determining whether any food is injurious to health, regard shall be had: (a) not only to the probable immediate and/or short-term and/or long-term effects of that food on the health of a person consuming it, but also on subsequent generations; (b) to the probable cumulative toxic effects; (c) to the particular health sensitivities of a specific category of consumers where the food is intended for that category of consumers. 5. In determining whether any food is unfit for human consumption, regard shall be had to whether the food is unacceptable for human consumption according to its intended use, for reasons of contamination, whether by extraneous matter or otherwise, or through putrefaction, deterioration or decay. 6. Where any food which is unsafe is part of a batch, lot or consignment of food of the same class or description, it shall be presumed that all the food in that batch, lot or consignment is also unsafe, unless following a detailed assessment there is no evidence that the rest of the batch, lot or consignment is unsafe. 7. final_output:
## 1. Short answer

If the applicable aflatoxin maximum is exceeded, the food generally **must not be placed on the market or used as a food ingredient**. Depending on when and where the exceedance is established, possible consequences include official-control measures against the consignment and, if the food has already entered the market, restrictions, withdrawal or recall.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

- **Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Article 2(1)** prohibits placing food listed in Annex I on the market, or using it as a raw material or ingredient, if it exceeds the applicable maximum level. Article 2(2) also prohibits mixing compliant food with food that exceeds the maximum.
- Under **Regulation (EU) 2017/625, Article 138**, where an official control establishes non-compliance, competent authorities may take appropriate measures. The listed possibilities include restricting or prohibiting placing goods on the market, ordering their treatment, and ordering their recall, withdrawal, removal or destruction. The authority must notify the operator of its decision and reasons.
- For food already distributed, **Regulation (EC) No 178/2002, Article 19(1)** requires a food business operator who considers, or has reason to believe, that food it handled does not comply with food-safety requirements to initiate withdrawal procedures and inform the competent authorities. If the food may have reached consumers, the operator must inform them; a consumer recall is required if necessary to achieve a high level of health protection.

These actions are not all automatic: the measure chosen depends on the circumstances and the competent authority’s assessment. Regulation 2023/915 also provides a specific route for certain food intended for sorting or other physical treatment, but only where the relevant Annex I provisions apply and their conditions are met (**Article 5**).

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

The exact maximum level and any sorting or processing route depend on the product’s classification and intended use. The question does not establish where the consignment is in the import or distribution process, or whether any special Annex I provision applies. The precise border-stage disposition should therefore be checked against the applicable import-control rules and current law; the available evidence does not establish that one particular outcome—such as re-dispatch or destruction—must follow in this case.
